subject: DI01000021

intro_text.en: Our own foundation chapter, written for students who reach diploma Mathematics-I without the school-level tools the GTU syllabus assumes. It rebuilds numbers and signs, fractions, LCM and GCD, BODMAS, indices and surds, standard form, algebraic expansion and factorisation, linear and simultaneous equations, quadratic equations, sets, ratio, percentage, averages and the coordinate plane - then adds a five-step study method and an exam plan. Twenty-two fully solved numericals, and every definition written in the same style as the official units. This chapter carries no GTU hours or marks.

h.en: 1.1 The number line and the families of numbers

body.en:
Definition

Every number you will use this semester sits on one line. Moving right adds, moving left subtracts, and the distance from zero is the absolute value |x|.

The families, from smallest to largest

FamilySymbolExamplesWhat it adds
NaturalN1, 2, 3, …Counting
WholeW0, 1, 2, 3, …Zero
IntegersZ…, −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, …Negative direction
RationalQ3/4, −2.5, 0.333…Every fraction of integers
IrrationalR − Q√2, π, eCannot be written as a fraction
RealRAll of the aboveEvery point on the line

Rules you will use daily

  • |−7| = 7 and |7| = 7: absolute value removes the sign.
  • On the line, −5 < −2 because −5 lies to the left.
  • A rational number has a terminating or repeating decimal; √2 = 1.41421… never repeats.
  • Between any two rational numbers there is another rational number - the line is dense, which is why graphs look continuous.
Is 0.75 rational?

Yes: 0.75 = 3/4, a fraction of integers.

Definition

Two signs next to each other combine into one: same signs give +, different signs give −. Then apply the operation.

Explanation and application

ExpressionCombineResult
(−3) + (+7) − (−2)−3 + 7 + 26
(−8) − (−5)−8 + 5−3
(−4) × (−3)same signs → positive12
(−12) ÷ (+4)different signs → negative−3
−2² vs (−2)²−2² = −(2×2); (−2)² = (−2)(−2)−4 vs 4

Common mistake / conditions

The last row decides many exam marks: −2² = −4 because the power applies to 2 only, while (−2)² = 4 because the bracket carries the sign. Write brackets when you mean them.

Definition

A fraction a/b means a parts out of b equal parts. It is simplified when no number except 1 divides both a and b.

The four operations

  1. Simplify: divide top and bottom by their GCD. 18/24 → 3/4.
  2. Add or subtract: take the LCM of the denominators, rewrite both fractions, then add the numerators: 5/6 + 3/4 = 10/12 + 9/12 = 19/12.
  3. Multiply: multiply tops and bottoms, then simplify: 5/6 × 9/10 = 45/60 = 3/4.
  4. Divide: flip the second fraction and multiply: 2/3 ÷ 4/9 = 2/3 × 9/4 = 18/12 = 3/2.

Common mistake / conditions

Denominators are never added: 5/6 + 3/4 is not 8/10. If the answer is bigger than 1, give it as a mixed number too - 19/12 = 1 7/12 - because that is how marks are usually written.

h.en: 1.4 GCD and LCM by prime factorisation

body.en:
Definition

GCD (HCF) is the largest number dividing both; LCM is the smallest number both divide. Prime factorisation gives both in one step.

Method

  1. Write each number as a product of primes: 48 = 2⁴ × 3 and 180 = 2² × 3² × 5.
  2. For the GCD take the common primes with the smallest powers: 2² × 3 = 12.
  3. For the LCM take every prime with the largest power: 2⁴ × 3² × 5 = 720.
  4. Check with GCD × LCM = product: 12 × 720 = 8640 = 48 × 180. ✓

Where it is used

Adding fractions (LCM of denominators), simplifying ratios, timing problems (two bells ring together again after the LCM of their intervals) and factorising algebraic expressions (GCD of coefficients).

Definition

A percentage is a fraction with denominator 100: 75 % = 75/100 = 0.75 = 3/4. An average (mean) divides a total equally among the count.

Three conversions you must do without thinking

  • Fraction → decimal: divide top by bottom (3/8 = 0.375).
  • Decimal → percentage: multiply by 100 (0.375 = 37.5 %).
  • Percentage → fraction: put over 100 and simplify (36 % = 9/25).

Application

15 % of 240 = 0.15 × 240 = 36. Increasing 240 by 15 % gives 240 + 36 = 276, which is the same as 240 × 1.15. Averages are used for internal marks and for reading graphs: the mean of 62, 78, 85 and 55 is 280/4 = 70.

title.en: 2. Order of Operations, Powers and Roots

h.en: 2.1 BODMAS: the only order that gives one answer

body.en:
Definition

An expression with several operations is evaluated in a fixed order: Brackets, Orders (powers and roots), Division and Multiplication (left to right), Addition and Subtraction (left to right).

Worked example

8 + 2 × (5 − 3)² = 8 + 2 × 2² = 8 + 2 × 4 = 8 + 8 = 16. Brackets first, then the power, then multiplication, then addition.

Common mistake / conditions

2 + 3 × 4 is 14, not 20: multiplication is done before addition. Similarly 12 ÷ 3 × 2 is 8, because division and multiplication are evaluated left to right - not 12 ÷ 6.

Definition

An index counts repeated multiplication: aⁿ = a × a × … (n times). The laws follow from that definition, so they never need to be memorised blindly.

The five laws

LawExampleReason
aᵐ × aⁿ = aᵐ⁺ⁿ2³ × 2⁴ = 2⁷count the factors
aᵐ ÷ aⁿ = aᵐ⁻ⁿ2⁵ ÷ 2² = 2³cancel common factors
(aᵐ)ⁿ = aᵐⁿ(2³)² = 2⁶three factors, repeated twice
a⁰ = 1 (a ≠ 0)7⁰ = 1aⁿ ÷ aⁿ = 1
a⁻ⁿ = 1/aⁿ2⁻³ = 1/8negative index means reciprocal

Application

In electronics, 10⁻⁶ means micro and 10³ means kilo; in units, m/s = m·s⁻¹. A fractional index is a root: a^(1/2) = √a and a^(2/3) = ∛(a²).

Definition

√a is the positive number whose square is a. A surd is a root that cannot be simplified to a whole number, such as √2 or 3√5.

Simplifying a surd

  1. Factor out the largest perfect square: √72 = √(36 × 2) = 6√2.
  2. Only like surds combine: √72 − √18 = 6√2 − 3√2 = 3√2 ≈ 4.243.
  3. Rationalise a denominator by multiplying top and bottom by the surd: 1/√2 = √2/2 ≈ 0.707.

Common mistake / conditions

√(a + b) is not √a + √b. For a = 9 and b = 16, √25 = 5 but 3 + 4 = 7. Check any rule with numbers before using it in an exam.

Definition

A number is in standard form when it is written as a × 10ⁿ with 1 ≤ a < 10. It keeps very large and very small engineering quantities readable.

Rules

  • Multiply: multiply the front numbers, add the powers - (3.6 × 10⁴)(2.5 × 10³) = 9.0 × 10⁷.
  • Divide: divide the front numbers, subtract the powers.
  • Add or subtract: make the powers equal first, then add - 3.6 × 10⁴ + 2.5 × 10³ = 36,000 + 2,500 = 38,500.
  • Move the decimal point right → smaller power; left → larger power.

A calculator display of 4.2E−3 means 4.2 × 10⁻³ = 0.0042, not 4200.

Definition

In 5x² − 3x + 7 the parts 5x², −3x and 7 are terms; 5 and −3 are coefficients; 7 is the constant. Only like terms (same letter, same power) may be combined.

Such a sum of terms with whole-number powers is a polynomial. Its highest power is the degree - 2 here, so it is a quadratic - and the degree tells you how many solutions the related equation can have: one for a linear polynomial, up to two for a quadratic, three for a cubic.

Explanation and application

  • 3x + 5x = 8x, but 3x + 5x² cannot be simplified - different powers.
  • Multiply powers by adding indices: x² · x³ = x⁵.
  • Substitution means replacing the letter by a number in brackets: 2x² − 3x + 1 at x = −2 is 2(−2)² − 3(−2) + 1 = 8 + 6 + 1 = 15.

Common mistake / conditions

Always put a negative value in brackets before substituting. Squaring without brackets gives −4 instead of 4 and the whole answer is wrong.

Definition

Expanding means multiplying every term of one bracket by every term of the other. Three patterns appear so often that they are worth knowing by sight.

The identities

IdentityExpanded formTypical use
(a + b)²a² + 2ab + b²(x + 4)² = x² + 8x + 16
(a − b)²a² − 2ab + b²(2a − 3b)² = 4a² − 12ab + 9b²
(a + b)(a − b)a² − b²(x + 5)(x − 5) = x² − 25

General expansion

(x + 3)(x − 5) = x² − 5x + 3x − 15 = x² − 2x − 15. The middle term is the sum of the cross products; that is why the sign matters.

Common mistake / conditions

(a + b)² is not a² + b². The middle term 2ab is the most frequently forgotten term in the paper.

Definition

Factorising writes a sum as a product. Always try the steps in this order.

Four-step checklist

  1. Common factor: 6x² + 9x = 3x(2x + 3).
  2. Difference of squares: 4x² − 25 = (2x − 5)(2x + 5).
  3. Quadratic trinomial: find two numbers whose product is c and sum is b. x² − 7x + 12 → −3 and −4 → (x − 3)(x − 4).
  4. Check by expanding: (x − 3)(x − 4) = x² − 7x + 12 ✓ - this check takes ten seconds and saves the whole question.

When the leading coefficient is not 1

For 2x² + 7x − 15, multiply 2 × (−15) = −30; find 10 and −3 (product −30, sum 7); split the middle term and group: 2x² + 10x − 3x − 15 = 2x(x + 5) − 3(x + 5) = (x + 5)(2x − 3).

Definition

Choosing the right first move is most of the work in algebra. Use this decision table before writing anything.

Decision table

Expression looks likeFirst move
Every term shares a factorTake the common factor out
Two squares with a minus betweena² − b² = (a + b)(a − b)
ax² + bx + c with a = 1Two numbers with product c, sum b
ax² + bx + c with a ≠ 1Split the middle term, then group
Fraction with a common factor on top and bottomFactorise both, then cancel

Why it matters later

Quadratic equations in Section 5, limits in Unit 5 and partial fractions in later semesters all begin with factorisation. A student who cannot factorise loses marks across the paper, not only in one question.

Definition

An equation is a balance. Whatever you do to one side you must do to the other, which is why moving a term across the equals sign changes its sign.

Worked example

3(x − 2) = 2x + 5 → 3x − 6 = 2x + 5 → 3x − 2x = 5 + 6 → x = 11.

The safe procedure

  1. Remove brackets.
  2. Collect the letter terms on one side and numbers on the other.
  3. Divide by the coefficient of the letter.
  4. Substitute the answer back into the original equation - both sides must agree.

Common mistake / conditions

Do not divide by a variable that could be zero, and never drop a minus sign while moving a term. The check step is not optional: 3(11 − 2) = 27 and 2(11) + 5 = 27 ✓.

h.en: 4.2 Turning a word problem into an equation

body.en:
Definition

Every word problem is a translation exercise: name the unknown, write the relation, solve, then answer the question that was asked.

Pattern: sum and difference

Two numbers add to 45 and differ by 9. Let them be x and x + 9 (because the difference is fixed). Then x + (x + 9) = 45 → 2x = 36 → x = 18, so the numbers are 18 and 27.

Pattern: ages, speeds, mixtures

  • Age problem: write both ages now, then add the same number of years to both.
  • Speed problem: distance = speed × time; keep the units consistent.
  • Mixture problem: track the amount of the substance, not only the volume.

Condition

State what the letter means before solving. "Let x be the number of pens" prevents the common error of finding a number and then reporting the wrong quantity.

Definition

A linear equation in two variables, such as 2x + 3y = 12, has infinitely many solutions on its own; two such equations are needed for two unknowns. Elimination removes one variable by adding or subtracting multiples of the equations; substitution replaces one variable using the other equation.

Worked example (substitution)

2x + 3y = 12 and x − y = 1. From the second, x = y + 1. Substitute: 2(y + 1) + 3y = 12 → 5y = 10 → y = 2, x = 3. Check: 2(3) + 3(2) = 12 ✓.

Worked example (elimination)

3p + 2q = 80 and 2p + 3q = 70. Multiply the first by 3 and the second by 2: 9p + 6q = 240 and 4p + 6q = 140. Subtract: 5p = 100 → p = 20, then q = 10.

Which to choose

Use substitution when one equation already gives a variable (x = …). Use elimination when both equations look alike - multiply to match the coefficients, then subtract.

h.en: 4.4 Checking, and what no solution means

body.en:
Definition

A pair of linear equations can meet once, never, or everywhere. The graph is two straight lines, and their relationship tells you the answer before you solve anything.

Three cases

CaseGraphAlgebraic signAnswer
One solutionLines cross onceDifferent slopesUnique (x, y)
No solutionParallel linesSame slope, different interceptInconsistent
Infinite solutionsSame lineOne equation is a multiple of the otherInfinitely many

Check routine

  1. Substitute the pair into both original equations.
  2. Confirm the units and answer the question in words.
  3. If a substitution fails, the algebra - not the method - is wrong; solve again slowly.

In the pens example, 3(20) + 2(10) = 80 and 2(20) + 3(10) = 70, so a pen is ₹20 and a pencil ₹10.

h.en: 5.1 Standard form and the three methods

body.en:
Definition

A quadratic equation has the form ax² + bx + c = 0 with a ≠ 0. It can have two, one or no real solutions, and its graph is a parabola.

Three methods

MethodUse it whenSpeed
FactorisationThe factors are obvious integersFastest, no calculator
Quadratic formulaAlwaysNever fails; needs care with signs
Completing the squareYou need the vertex or a proofSlow, shows the structure

Before choosing

Write the equation in standard form first. 3x(x − 2) = 15 must become 3x² − 6x − 15 = 0 (or x² − 2x − 5 = 0) before any method is applied.

Definition

If two factors multiply to zero, at least one of them is zero. That single idea turns a quadratic into two linear equations.

Worked examples

x² − 5x + 6 = 0 → (x − 2)(x − 3) = 0 → x = 2 or x = 3.

2x² + 7x − 15 = 0 → (2x − 3)(x + 5) = 0 → x = 3/2 or x = −5.

Procedure for a ≠ 1

  1. Multiply a and c: 2 × (−15) = −30.
  2. Find two numbers with product −30 and sum 7: 10 and −3.
  3. Split the middle term, group and factorise.
  4. Set each bracket to zero and solve.

Common mistake / conditions

(2x − 3) = 0 gives x = 3/2, not 3. Divide by the coefficient of x inside the bracket, and check both roots in the original equation.

h.en: 5.3 The quadratic formula and the discriminant

body.en:
Formula

For ax² + bx + c = 0, x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac)) / 2a, and D = b² − 4ac is the discriminant.

What D tells you before you finish

DRootsGraph
D > 0Two distinct real rootsParabola cuts the x-axis twice
D = 0One repeated root, x = −b/2aParabola touches the x-axis
D < 0No real rootsParabola stays above or below the axis

Worked example

3x² − 4x + 5 = 0: D = (−4)² − 4(3)(5) = 16 − 60 = −44. D < 0, so there is no real solution - do not force the formula and invent a root.

Check with the sum and product

The roots satisfy x₁ + x₂ = −b/a and x₁x₂ = c/a. For 2x² + 7x − 15: sum = −7/2 = 1.5 + (−5) ✓ and product = −15/2 = 1.5 × (−5) ✓.

Definition

Any situation with an area, a product, or a squared unknown produces a quadratic. The physical meaning then decides which root to keep.

Worked example

A rectangle is 5 m longer than it is wide and its area is 84 m². Let the width be w; then w(w + 5) = 84 → w² + 5w − 84 = 0 → (w + 12)(w − 7) = 0 → w = 7 or w = −12.

Choosing the root

A length cannot be negative, so w = −12 is rejected. Width = 7 m, length = 12 m, and 7 × 12 = 84 ✓. Always state the rejected root and why.

Definition

A set is a collection of distinct objects. If A = {1, 2, 3, 4} and B = {3, 4, 5}, then the three operations give:

OperationMeaningAnswer for A and BCount
A ∪ B (union)Everything in A or B{1, 2, 3, 4, 5}5
A ∩ B (intersection)Only what is in both{3, 4}2
A − B (difference)In A but not in B{1, 2}2

Why it is in the prerequisite list

Domain and range in Unit 1, solution sets of inequalities, and probability in later semesters are all written in set notation. The counting rule n(A ∪ B) = n(A) + n(B) − n(A ∩ B) explains double counting: 4 + 3 − 2 = 5 ✓.

Definition

A ratio compares parts of the same whole; a proportion says two ratios are equal (a : b = c : d, so ad = bc).

Dividing an amount in a ratio

  1. Add the ratio parts: 2 + 3 + 4 = 9.
  2. One part = total / 9 = 4500 / 9 = 500.
  3. Multiply: 2 × 500 = 1000, 3 × 500 = 1500, 4 × 500 = 2000.
  4. Check: 1000 + 1500 + 2000 = 4500 ✓.

Application

Mixing concrete 1 : 2 : 4, dividing profit between partners, scaling a map or a drawing, and resolving a force into components all use the same arithmetic.

Definition

Percentage change compares the change with the original value: change % = (new − old)/old × 100.

Worked examples

  • Price 800 → 920: change = +120, so 120/800 × 100 = +15 %.
  • Price 920 → 800: change = −120, and the original is now 920, so 120/920 × 100 = −13.04 %.
  • A 15 % rise followed by a 15 % fall does not return to the start: 800 × 1.15 × 0.85 = 782.

Common mistake / conditions

Always divide by the value before the change, and remember that successive percentages multiply. The GST-style question "price before tax" is a reverse percentage: divide by (1 + rate), do not subtract the rate from the final price.

Definition

Mean = sum of values / number of values. It is the balance point of the data, and the only average you need this semester.

Worked example

Marks 62, 78, 85, 55: sum = 280, count = 4, mean = 70. If the next test is 90, the new mean is 370/5 = 74 - one high score lifts the average by 4 marks.

Limitation

A single extreme value pulls the mean. The median (middle value when sorted) is safer for salaries or house prices. State which average you used and why.

h.en: 7.1 Axes, quadrants and plotting a point

body.en:
Definition

Two perpendicular number lines give every point a unique address (x, y): x is measured along the horizontal axis, y along the vertical axis.

The four quadrants

QuadrantxyExample
Ipositivepositive(3, 2)
IInegativepositive(−4, 3)
IIInegativenegative(−2, −5)
IVpositivenegative(6, −1)

Rules

  • A point on the x-axis has y = 0; on the y-axis x = 0; the origin is (0, 0).
  • Plot by counting along x first, then along y - in that order.
  • Always write the bracket and the comma; (3, 2) and (2, 3) are different points.

This section is the bridge to Unit 4: distance, midpoint and slope are all measured on this grid.

Formula

For A(x₁, y₁) and B(x₂, y₂): AB = √((x₂ − x₁)² + (y₂ − y₁)²) - Pythagoras on the horizontal and vertical gaps.

Worked example

A(2, 3) and B(6, 6): gaps are 4 and 3, so AB = √(16 + 9) = √25 = 5 units.

Checks that catch errors

  • Distance is never negative; a negative answer means a sign slip.
  • Order does not matter, because both gaps are squared.
  • If the points share an x or a y, the distance is simply the other gap.

Application

Length of a side of a plot, distance between two machines on a layout, error between a measured point and a nominal point.

Formulae

Midpoint M = ((x₁ + x₂)/2, (y₁ + y₂)/2). Slope m = (y₂ − y₁)/(x₂ − x₁) = rise / run.

Worked example

A(2, 3) and B(6, 6): midpoint = (4, 4.5) and slope = (6 − 3)/(6 − 2) = 3/4 = 0.75. A line rising 3 units for every 4 to the right.

Reading the slope

SlopeMeaning
positiveline rises left to right
negativeline falls left to right
zerohorizontal line
undefinedvertical line (x₂ = x₁)

Slope is the first thing Unit 4 asks for: it appears in the two-point form, the slope-point form, the parallel and perpendicular conditions, and the tangent to a circle.

title.en: 8. How to Study Mathematics: The Five-Step Method

body.en:
The method

Mathematics is learnt by doing, not by reading. Use the same five steps for every topic in this subject.

  1. Read a solved example with a pen in hand: cover the solution, predict the next line, then check.
  2. Copy it closed-book immediately, then compare line by line. Any line you cannot reproduce is the line you did not understand.
  3. Change the numbers and solve the same skeleton again - same method, your values.
  4. Attempt an unsolved problem and write every step, even the wrong ones.
  5. Log the error in one line ("moved −3 without changing sign") and revise it after 1 day, 1 week and 1 month.

Why it works

Steps 1-2 build recognition, step 3 builds transfer, step 4 exposes gaps, and step 5 stops the same mistake from returning in the exam.

h.en: 8.2 A weekly routine that fits a diploma timetable

body.en:
The plan

  • 20 minutes daily: one numerical from the current unit, written fully.
  • Twice a week: five viva answers spoken aloud - speaking exposes fake understanding.
  • Once a week: one timed 12-mark set from the Exam tab, closed book.
  • Before a test: re-solve only the questions in your error log, not the whole chapter.

How to use this app

  1. Open the unit, read a card, then close it and say the definition aloud.
  2. Open the gold EX box only after trying the numerical yourself.
  3. Use Viva for one-line answers and Exam Qs for written practice.
  4. Check your answer against the "Interpretation and check" line; a right number with no check is half an answer.

Condition

Do not read mathematics like a story. If your pen has not moved in five minutes, you are not studying - you are watching.

Before you write

  • Read the whole paper once and mark the questions you can finish (usually 60-70 % of it).
  • Attempt in order of confidence, not in order of the paper.
  • For each question, write the formula first - formula marks are awarded even if arithmetic fails.

During the paper

  1. Show every step; a correct answer with no working loses method marks.
  2. Carry units and brackets; write the final answer as a sentence with units.
  3. Leave 5 minutes for arithmetic checks and for unanswered one-mark parts.

Where the marks are

The official specification splits 70 marks as R 19, U 27, A 24 - more than half the paper is understanding and application. Memorising definitions alone cannot reach a pass.

Working

  1. (−3) × 2 = −6 (multiplication before addition)
  2. (−8) + 5 = −3
  3. −3 + (−6) = −9

Answer

−9. Check by counting on the number line from −8: right 5 → −3, left 6 → −9.

Working

  1. LCM(8, 6) = 24
  2. 3/8 = 9/24 and 5/6 = 20/24
  3. 9/24 + 20/24 = 29/24

Answer

29/24 = 1 5/24 ≈ 1.208. Both fractions are close to 1/2 and 5/6 is close to 1, so an answer near 1.2 is expected; 8/14 - adding the tops and the bottoms - is the classic wrong answer and does not even keep the size of the number.

h.en: Practice 3. Find the GCD and LCM of 36 and 60.

body.en:
Working

  1. 36 = 2² × 3²
  2. 60 = 2² × 3 × 5
  3. GCD = 2² × 3 = 12
  4. LCM = 2² × 3² × 5 = 180

Check

12 × 180 = 2160 = 36 × 60 ✓. The GCD is a factor of both numbers and the LCM is a multiple of both: 36 = 12 × 3 and 60 = 12 × 5, while 180/36 = 5 and 180/60 = 3 - the cross-values match, which is a quick second check.

Working

  1. (4 − 1)² = 9
  2. 12 ÷ 3 = 4, then 4 × 2 = 8 (left to right)
  3. 8 + 9 = 17

Answer

17. Dividing as 12 ÷ 6 = 2 is the classic wrong path: division and multiplication have equal priority, so they are read left to right. A calculator entered as 12 ÷ 3 × 2 also returns 8, which is a fast way to confirm the order.

Working

Collect like terms: (3x² + 2x²) + (−5x − x) + 7 = 5x² − 6x + 7. Nothing else combines, because 5x², −6x and 7 are unlike terms.

Answer

5x² − 6x + 7. Check by substituting x = 2: the original expression gives 12 − 10 + 8 + 7 − 2 = 15, and 5(4) − 12 + 7 = 15 ✓. A substitution check works for any simplification question.

Working

Two numbers with product 20 and sum −9: −4 and −5, because (−4)(−5) = 20 and (−4) + (−5) = −9. Therefore x² − 9x + 20 = (x − 4)(x − 5).

Check

Expanding gives x² − 5x − 4x + 20 = x² − 9x + 20 ✓, so the roots of the related equation would be x = 4 and x = 5.

Working

  1. 5x + 5 = 3x + 17
  2. 5x − 3x = 17 − 5
  3. 2x = 12
  4. x = 6

Check

Left: 5(6 + 1) = 35. Right: 3(6) + 17 = 35 ✓. Both sides agree, so x = 6 is correct; divide by the coefficient only at the last step, never before collecting the terms.

Working

  1. From the second equation, x = y + 2
  2. 3(y + 2) + 2y = 16
  3. 5y + 6 = 16 → y = 2
  4. x = 2 + 2 = 4

Check

3(4) + 2(2) = 16 ✓ and 4 − 2 = 2 ✓. The lines have different slopes (−3/2 and 1), so exactly one pair (4, 2) exists - the answer is consistent with the geometry.

h.en: Practice 10. Solve x² + 2x − 8 = 0 and state the nature of the roots.

body.en:
Working

Two numbers with product −8 and sum 2 are 4 and −2, so x² + 2x − 8 = (x + 4)(x − 2) = 0, giving x = −4 or x = 2. Independently, D = 2² − 4(1)(−8) = 36 > 0, which confirms two distinct real roots.

Check

Sum = −4 + 2 = −2 = −b/a ✓ and product = (−4)(2) = −8 = c/a ✓. Because a > 0 the parabola opens upward and cuts the x-axis at −4 and 2.

h.en: Practice 11. A number plus its square is 30. Find the number.

body.en:
Working

x + x² = 30 → x² + x − 30 = 0 → (x + 6)(x − 5) = 0 → x = 5 or x = −6.

Answer

Both satisfy the words: 5 + 25 = 30 and −6 + 36 = 30. Unless the question says "positive number", give both.

h.en: Practice 12. Find the distance, midpoint and slope for P(1, 2) and Q(7, 10).

body.en:
Working

  1. Gaps: 6 and 8
  2. PQ = √(36 + 64) = 10
  3. Midpoint = (4, 6)
  4. Slope = 8/6 = 4/3 ≈ 1.33

Check

(6 − 2)/(4 − 1) = 4/3, the same slope from the midpoint ✓.

h.en: Practice 13. What is 18 % of 250, and what is 250 increased by 18 %?

body.en:
Working

  1. 18 % = 0.18
  2. 0.18 × 250 = 45
  3. 250 + 45 = 295, and 250 × 1.18 = 295

Answer

45 and 295. Note the difference between the two parts of the question: "18 % of 250" is the part, while "increased by 18 %" is the new whole. GST of 18 % on a ₹250 item is added the same way.

h.en: Practice 14. A sum of ₹6,000 is divided in the ratio 3 : 5. Find both shares.

body.en:
Working

  1. Sum of parts = 3 + 5 = 8
  2. One part = 6000 / 8 = ₹750
  3. Shares = 3 × 750 = ₹2,250 and 5 × 750 = ₹3,750

Check

2250 + 3750 = 6000 ✓, and dividing both shares by 750 returns 3 : 5 ✓. State the answer with the rupee symbol and a comma for thousands, as a marker expects.

title.en: The number line and absolute value

terms.en: The middle term 2ab is the one most often forgotten.
Sign of the middle term follows the bracket.
Use it in both directions: expand and factorise.
Find two numbers whose sum is the middle coefficient and product is the constant.
Always arrange the equation in this form before choosing a method.
Works for every quadratic; substitute signs carefully.
D > 0: two real roots; D = 0: one repeated root; D < 0: no real root.
Fastest check of a factorisation or of the formula.
Find both from prime factorisation: common primes (smallest) and all primes (largest).
Divide by the value before the change; successive changes multiply.
Sensitive to extreme values; the median is safer for skewed data.

items.f: one part = total / sum of ratio parts

terms.en: Multiply one part by each ratio term and check the total.
Pythagoras on the horizontal and vertical gaps.
Average the x-coordinates and the y-coordinates separately.
Rise over run; vertical line (x₂ = x₁) has no finite slope.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Two signs together combine first: same signs give +, different signs give −.

Formula

a − (−b) = a + b and a + (−b) = a − b

Step-by-step solution

  1. (−3) + (+7) = 4
  2. 4 − (−2) = 4 + 2
  3. = 6

Interpretation and check

6. Sanity: starting at −3, moving 7 right reaches 4, then 2 more right reaches 6.

q.en: Add 5/6 + 3/4 and give the answer as a mixed number.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Denominators 6 and 4; LCM(6, 4) = 12.

Formula

a/b + c/d = (ad + bc)/bd, then simplify

Step-by-step solution

  1. 5/6 = 10/12 and 3/4 = 9/12
  2. 10/12 + 9/12 = 19/12
  3. 19/12 = 1 7/12

Interpretation and check

19/12 ≈ 1.583. Estimate 0.833 + 0.75 = 1.583 ✓ - the answer must be close to the estimate.

Given and assumptions

Dividing by a fraction is multiplying by its reciprocal.

Formula

a/b ÷ c/d = a/b × d/c

Step-by-step solution

  1. 2/3 × 9/4
  2. = 18/12
  3. = 3/2 = 1.5

Interpretation and check

3/2. Check by multiplication: (3/2)(4/9) = 12/18 = 2/3 ✓.

q.en: Find the GCD and LCM of 48 and 180.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Prime factorisation of both numbers.

Formula

GCD = common primes, smallest powers; LCM = all primes, largest powers

Step-by-step solution

  1. 48 = 2⁴ × 3
  2. 180 = 2² × 3² × 5
  3. GCD = 2² × 3 = 12
  4. LCM = 2⁴ × 3² × 5 = 720

Interpretation and check

GCD 12, LCM 720. Check GCD × LCM = 12 × 720 = 8640 = 48 × 180 ✓.

q.en: Find 15 % of 240, and the value after a 15 % increase.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Base value 240; rate 15 %.

Formula

part = rate × base; increased value = base × (1 + rate)

Step-by-step solution

  1. 15 % = 0.15
  2. 0.15 × 240 = 36
  3. 240 + 36 = 276, or 240 × 1.15 = 276

Interpretation and check

36 and 276. Check: 10 % of 240 is 24 and 5 % is 12, so 15 % is 36 ✓.

q.en: Evaluate 8 + 2 × (5 − 3)².

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Apply BODMAS: brackets, orders, multiplication, addition.

Formula

B → O → D/M left to right → A/S left to right

Step-by-step solution

  1. (5 − 3) = 2
  2. 2² = 4
  3. 2 × 4 = 8
  4. 8 + 8 = 16

Interpretation and check

16. The common wrong answer 100 comes from squaring 8 + 2 first, which ignores the brackets.

q.en: Simplify (2³ × 2⁻⁵) ÷ 2⁻¹.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Laws of indices with the same base 2.

Formula

aᵐ × aⁿ = aᵐ⁺ⁿ and aᵐ ÷ aⁿ = aᵐ⁻ⁿ

Step-by-step solution

  1. 2³ × 2⁻⁵ = 2⁻²
  2. 2⁻² ÷ 2⁻¹ = 2⁻² ⁺ ¹ = 2⁻¹
  3. 2⁻¹ = 1/2

Interpretation and check

1/2 = 0.5. Check numerically: (8 × 1/32) ÷ (1/2) = (1/4) × 2 = 1/2 ✓.

q.en: Simplify √72 − √18, and give the decimal value.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Extract the largest perfect square from each surd.

Formula

√(a²b) = a√b

Step-by-step solution

  1. √72 = √(36 × 2) = 6√2
  2. √18 = √(9 × 2) = 3√2
  3. 6√2 − 3√2 = 3√2 = 3 × 1.41421 = 4.243

Interpretation and check

3√2 ≈ 4.243. Check: 6 × 1.414 = 8.485 and 3 × 1.414 = 4.243; the difference is 4.243 ✓.

q.en: Multiply (3.6 × 10⁴) by (2.5 × 10³) and write the answer in standard form.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Front numbers and powers handled separately.

Formula

(a × 10ᵐ)(b × 10ⁿ) = ab × 10ᵐ⁺ⁿ

Step-by-step solution

  1. 3.6 × 2.5 = 9.0
  2. 10⁴ × 10³ = 10⁷
  3. = 9.0 × 10⁷ = 90,000,000

Interpretation and check

9.0 × 10⁷. Estimate 4 × 10⁴ × 2.5 × 10³ = 10 × 10⁷ = 1 × 10⁸, so 9 × 10⁷ is right.

q.en: Evaluate 2x² − 3x + 1 at x = −2.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Substitute the negative value inside brackets.

Formula

Replace x by (−2) everywhere, then apply BODMAS

Step-by-step solution

  1. 2(−2)² − 3(−2) + 1
  2. = 2(4) + 6 + 1
  3. = 8 + 6 + 1 = 15

Interpretation and check

15. The common error is writing −2² for (−2)², which gives 8 − 6 + 1 = 3 instead of 15.

q.en: Expand (x + 3)(x − 5).

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Two binomials; multiply every term of the first by every term of the second.

Formula

(x + a)(x + b) = x² + (a + b)x + ab

Step-by-step solution

  1. x(x − 5) = x² − 5x
  2. 3(x − 5) = 3x − 15
  3. x² − 5x + 3x − 15 = x² − 2x − 15

Interpretation and check

x² − 2x − 15. Check with x = 1: LHS (4)(−4) = −16; RHS 1 − 2 − 15 = −16 ✓.

q.en: Factorise 2x² + 7x − 15 and solve 2x² + 7x − 15 = 0.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

a = 2, b = 7, c = −15; product a·c = −30.

Formula

Find two numbers with product a·c and sum b, split the middle term, group

Step-by-step solution

  1. 10 × (−3) = −30 and 10 + (−3) = 7
  2. 2x² + 10x − 3x − 15 = 2x(x + 5) − 3(x + 5)
  3. = (x + 5)(2x − 3)
  4. x + 5 = 0 → x = −5; 2x − 3 = 0 → x = 3/2

Interpretation and check

(x + 5)(2x − 3), roots −5 and 3/2. Sum = −7/2 = −b/a ✓; product = −15/2 = c/a ✓.

q.en: Solve 3(x − 2) = 2x + 5.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

One variable, one equation; remove the bracket first.

Formula

The same operation on both sides keeps the balance

Step-by-step solution

  1. 3x − 6 = 2x + 5
  2. 3x − 2x = 5 + 6
  3. x = 11

Interpretation and check

x = 11. Check: 3(11 − 2) = 27 and 2(11) + 5 = 27 ✓.

q.en: Solve 2x + 3y = 12 and x − y = 1.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Two equations, two unknowns; substitution is easiest because the second gives x.

Formula

x = y + 1 from the second equation

Step-by-step solution

  1. 2(y + 1) + 3y = 12
  2. 2y + 2 + 3y = 12
  3. 5y = 10 → y = 2
  4. x = 2 + 1 = 3

Interpretation and check

x = 3, y = 2. Check both: 2(3) + 3(2) = 12 ✓ and 3 − 2 = 1 ✓.

q.en: Three pens and two pencils cost ₹80; two pens and three pencils cost ₹70. Find the price of each.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Let a pen cost p and a pencil q. The words become two equations.

Formula

3p + 2q = 80 and 2p + 3q = 70

Step-by-step solution

  1. Multiply the first by 3: 9p + 6q = 240
  2. Multiply the second by 2: 4p + 6q = 140
  3. Subtract: 5p = 100 → p = 20
  4. Then 3(20) + 2q = 80 → q = 10

Interpretation and check

Pen ₹20, pencil ₹10. Check the second equation: 2(20) + 3(10) = 70 ✓. Always answer in words with units.

q.en: Solve 3x² − 4x + 5 = 0 and comment on the roots.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

a = 3, b = −4, c = 5.

Formula

x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac)) / 2a; D = b² − 4ac

Step-by-step solution

  1. D = (−4)² − 4(3)(5) = 16 − 60 = −44
  2. D < 0, so √D is not a real number
  3. No real solution exists

Interpretation and check

D = −44, no real roots. The correct conclusion is "no real roots", not "x = 0". The parabola y = 3x² − 4x + 5 stays above the x-axis.

q.en: A rectangle is 5 m longer than it is wide and has area 84 m². Find its dimensions.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Let width = w metres, so length = w + 5 metres.

Formula

area = width × length

Step-by-step solution

  1. w(w + 5) = 84
  2. w² + 5w − 84 = 0
  3. (w + 12)(w − 7) = 0
  4. w = 7 or w = −12

Interpretation and check

7 m × 12 m. A width cannot be negative, so −12 is rejected; 7 × 12 = 84 ✓.

q.en: Divide ₹4,500 in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Total 4500; ratio parts 2, 3 and 4.

Formula

one part = total / sum of parts

Step-by-step solution

  1. Sum of parts = 9
  2. One part = 4500 / 9 = 500
  3. Shares = 1000, 1500, 2000

Interpretation and check

₹1,000, ₹1,500 and ₹2,000. Check the total: 1000 + 1500 + 2000 = 4500 ✓.

q.en: A price rises from ₹800 to ₹920 and later falls back to ₹800. Find both percentage changes.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Percentage change is measured against the original value each time.

Formula

change % = (new − old)/old × 100

Step-by-step solution

  1. Rise: (920 − 800)/800 × 100 = 15 %
  2. Fall: (800 − 920)/920 × 100 = −13.04 %
  3. Net: 800 × 1.15 × 0.8696 = 800 (back to the start only because 920 → 800 is a different base)

Interpretation and check

+15 % then −13.04 %. The two percentages are not equal because the bases differ - this is the classic successive-percentage trap.

q.en: For A(2, 3) and B(6, 6) find the distance AB, the midpoint and the slope of AB.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

x₁ = 2, y₁ = 3 and x₂ = 6, y₂ = 6; gaps are 4 and 3.

Formula

AB = √((x₂−x₁)² + (y₂−y₁)²); M = ((x₁+x₂)/2, (y₁+y₂)/2); m = (y₂−y₁)/(x₂−x₁)

Step-by-step solution

  1. AB = √(4² + 3²) = √25 = 5
  2. M = (8/2, 9/2) = (4, 4.5)
  3. m = 3/4 = 0.75

Interpretation and check

AB = 5, midpoint (4, 4.5), slope 0.75. Check slope with the midpoint: (4.5 − 3)/(4 − 2) = 1.5/2 = 0.75 ✓.

q.en: If A = {1, 2, 3, 4} and B = {3, 4, 5}, find n(A ∪ B), A ∩ B and A − B.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Two sets with two elements in common.

Formula

n(A ∪ B) = n(A) + n(B) − n(A ∩ B)

Step-by-step solution

  1. A ∩ B = {3, 4}, so n(A ∩ B) = 2
  2. n(A ∪ B) = 4 + 3 − 2 = 5, and indeed A ∪ B = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}
  3. A − B = {1, 2}

Interpretation and check

5, {3, 4} and {1, 2}. Check the parts: 1 and 2 only in A (2 elements), 3 and 4 in both (2), 5 only in B (1) → 2 + 2 + 1 = 5 ✓.

q.en: The marks of a student are 62, 78, 85 and 55. Find the mean. What is the new mean if the next test is 90?

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Four values, then five values after the next test.

Formula

mean = sum of values / count

Step-by-step solution

  1. Sum = 62 + 78 + 85 + 55 = 280
  2. Mean = 280 / 4 = 70
  3. After 90: (280 + 90) / 5 = 370 / 5 = 74

Interpretation and check

70, then 74. Check the change: the new value is 20 above the old mean, so the mean rises by 20/5 = 4 ✓.

q.en: Is every integer a rational number?

a.en: Yes: any integer n can be written as n/1.

q.en: What is the difference between GCD and LCM?

a.en: GCD is the largest number dividing both values; LCM is the smallest number both values divide.

q.en: How do you add two fractions with different denominators?

a.en: Take the LCM of the denominators, rewrite both fractions over it, then add the numerators.

q.en: State the BODMAS order.

a.en: Brackets, Orders (powers and roots), Division and Multiplication left to right, Addition and Subtraction left to right.

q.en: What is a⁻ⁿ?

a.en: The reciprocal of aⁿ: a⁻ⁿ = 1/aⁿ, so 2⁻³ = 1/8.

q.en: What is a surd?

a.en: An irrational root such as √2 or 3√5 that cannot be simplified to a whole number.

q.en: Expand (a + b)².

a.en: a² + 2ab + b² - the middle term must not be dropped.

q.en: Factorise a² − b².

a.en: (a + b)(a − b), the difference of two squares.

q.en: How do you factorise 2x² + 7x − 15?

a.en: Split the middle term using numbers with product −30 and sum 7 (10 and −3), group, then write (x + 5)(2x − 3).

q.en: What does it mean if a quadratic has D < 0?

a.en: The equation has no real roots; the parabola does not meet the x-axis.

q.en: Give the quadratic formula.

a.en: x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac)) / 2a for ax² + bx + c = 0.

q.en: Why do you substitute the answer back into the equation?

a.en: To verify the solution satisfies the original equation and to catch sign or arithmetic errors.

q.en: When do two linear equations have no solution?

a.en: When their slopes are equal but intercepts differ, that is the lines are parallel.

q.en: Which method is faster for x − y = 1 and 2x + 3y = 12?

a.en: Substitution, because the first equation already gives x = y + 1.

q.en: In a rectangle word problem, why is the negative root rejected?

a.en: Because a physical length cannot be negative; state the rejection explicitly.

q.en: How do you divide an amount in a given ratio?

a.en: Divide the total by the sum of the ratio parts, then multiply by each part.

q.en: Why is a 15 % rise followed by a 15 % fall not a return to the original price?

a.en: The percentages are taken on different bases; the factors 1.15 and 0.85 multiply to 0.9775.

q.en: What is A ∩ B?

a.en: The set of elements present in both A and B.

q.en: State the distance formula.

a.en: AB = √((x₂ − x₁)² + (y₂ − y₁)²).

q.en: What does a slope of zero mean?

a.en: The line is horizontal: y does not change as x changes.

q.en: Why is the mean not always a good average?

a.en: A single extreme value can pull it far from the typical value; the median resists this.

learning_outcomes.en: Use fractions, powers, roots and standard form without a calculator.
Expand and factorise algebraic expressions, and check the result by expanding back.
Solve linear, simultaneous and quadratic equations, including word problems.
Work with sets, ratio, percentage and averages in engineering contexts.
Read the coordinate plane and compute distance, midpoint and slope.
